messages:
alex_g: Quick follow-up from yesterday's whiteboard: propose an "SLA token" header that encodes client preference (latency vs cost) + soft region hints so router can do a very cheap short-circuit. Not a policy override, advisory only.

maya: important: advisory only. we need to be explicit in docs. Also keep backward compat (no header = neutral).

ravi: perf: parsing must be O(1). prefer small binary with flags + 1 byte bucket for bias + 1 byte region id. base64 in header `x-rdw-slatoken`. Avoid JSON.

pri: suggested wire: v1 | flags(8bit) | bias(0..255) | region_id(8bit). bias maps to quantized buckets used by fast-path table.

sam: runtime plan: header parser lives in edge proxy, convert to compact struct, forward to policy engine. Policy engine implements two-tier eval: fast-path O(1) table lookup using (region_id, flags_bucket) -> candidate route. If confidence low, run full policy graph.

maya: confidence metric = top_score - second_score; tuneable threshold. Also add sampled full-eval fallback to measure drift.

pri: telemetry: every decision annotated with token_present, token_bucket, fastpath_used, confidence_delta, fallback_reason. export to route-telemetry pipeline.

ravi: testing: add replayer that injects tokens into production traces to measure cost and misroute rate. Also fuzz tokens to ensure safety.

sam: rollout: feature-flag + dry-run scoring -> canary 5-10% tenants -> gate on no P95 regressions and token-influenced cost delta within budget -> 100%.

alex_g: security: validate token region ids against tenant allowed regions; treat malformed tokens as neutral. rate-limit parse CPU.

opsbot: Created backlog issue RDW-ARCH-321 for schema, sim harness, telemetry.

alex_g: Action items: ravi/prio to sketch fast-path table API; maya to define telemetry names; sam to add header parser + feature flag. We'll reconvene next Tue.
